# How to use this file

This is the **long-term refactor**: the target architecture and the correct
epidemiology, to be implemented *after* the MVP (`01_..._MVP_2026-07-23.Rmd`) has
shipped a defensible 7/23 run. Paste sections into Claude Code as you work through
them. All code blocks are `eval=FALSE` — they are edit instructions, not runnable
chunks.

**Guiding principle.** The current pipeline has the right *foundation* (source-split
sodium, multiplicative composition of overlapping interventions) but collapses
everything into a single **static, country-level `salteff` scalar**. The requested
changes need effects that vary by **country × year × source × intervention ×
target population**. The refactor preserves the downstream disease model
(incidence, case-fatality, state transitions) and replaces the upstream scalar with
a transparent, year-specific intervention engine, plus reproducibility scaffolding.

**Do not start this until:** (a) MVP results are shared, and (b) MVP outputs are
frozen under `output/out_model/legacy_static/` so the refactor can be proven
result-preserving under a `legacy_static` config before new assumptions are turned
on.

# Target file responsibilities

The refactor gives each script a single clear job. Current problems noted inline.

## `00_run_model.R` — configuration + orchestration only

Move *all* user-controlled parameters here and pass a single config object into
functions. The current runner embeds machine-specific Windows paths and separate
working directories, which makes reproduction and parallel execution fragile.

```r
# Model horizon (currently hard-coded as a 41-step 2017->2058 loop in 07)
MODEL_START_YEAR <- 2026L
MODEL_END_YEAR   <- 2050L

# Policy ramp
POLICY_START_YEAR <- 2026L
POLICY_FULL_YEAR  <- 2030L

COUNTRIES <- c("Viet Nam","Philippines","Bangladesh","China","Ethiopia",
               "India","Malaysia","Thailand","Cameroon","Nigeria")

INTERVENTIONS <- c("public_procurement","fopl","salt_targets","fiscal",
                   "lss_diagnosed_htn","lss_treated_htn")  # + lss_all if scenario 2 retained

INCLUDE_MEDIA               <- FALSE
INCLUDE_LSS_IN_FULL_PACKAGE <- FALSE

PACKAGED_TREND_METHOD     <- "euromonitor_prediction_apc"  # 2025-2030
PACKAGED_TREND_AFTER_2030 <- "hold_constant"               # "compound_capped" = sensitivity

FISCAL_METHOD <- "fixed_effect"   # or "elasticity"
LSS_METHOD    <- "trial_rr"       # or "sodium_sbp_sensitivity"

ADULT_POPULATION_ONLY <- TRUE

# Use project-relative paths, create output dirs, source scripts in order,
# pass config downstream.
library(here)   # replace the hard-coded OneDrive path
```

## `05_build_baseline.R` — policy-free baseline

Build epidemiological baseline rates and the natural-history projection using the
config horizon. **No intervention assumptions.** The state-transition loop is

## `07_run_interventions.R` — scenario runner only

After refactor: receive processed inputs + config; create country-specific
scenarios; compute year-specific source reductions; translate to SBP or direct
outcome effects; call the existing disease model; save results **plus an

---

# The year-specific intervention engine

Replace the single scalar with an explicit decomposition applied per country,
year, source, intervention, and target population:

```r
# annual_contribution(s,t) =
#   source_share(s,t) * full_effect(s) * implementation_fraction(t)
#
# total_reduction(c,t) = sum_over_sources( annual_contribution(s,t) )
#
# Overlapping policies on the same source compose multiplicatively:
#   composed_effect(s,t) = 1 - prod_i( 1 - eff_i,s(t) )
#
# The source trend (packaged growth) and the policy ramp are applied SEPARATELY
# and must not be conflated.
```

`total_reduction(c,t)` is the year-varying analogue of the old `salteff` and feeds
the existing `calculate_sodium_impact_etihad()` per year rather than once.

---

# Euromonitor packaged-food trend module

The workbook has: all-observed 2011–2025 (AAPC + linear trend); post-COVID
2023–2025; predicted 2025–2030 (APC + linear trend), by packaged-food category.

**Base case — predicted APC, matches the policy period:**

```r
# I(c,t) = (1 + g_c)^(t - 2025), for 2025 <= t <= 2030
# g_c = country-specific packaged-food growth rate.
# After 2030: hold I constant in the PRIMARY analysis.
# Compound growth through 2050 is a SENSITIVITY only, and must be capped.
```

**Category aggregation — do not average all rows.** Parent and child categories
coexist (Meals and Soups / Ready Meals / Soup; Dairy / Cheese); including both
double-counts.

```r
# Preferred : non-overlapping LEAF categories, weighted by 2025 sales volume and,
#             ideally, category-specific sodium density.
# Interim   : median APC across selected non-overlapping categories.
# Sensitivity: post-COVID APC and full-observation AAPC.
```

**Update source shares as composition, not automatic total-intake growth
(primary):**

```r
# w_packaged(c,t) = [ w_packaged(c,2025) * I(c,t) ]
#   / [ w_packaged(c,2025) * I(c,t) + sum(non-packaged shares) ]
# Renormalise remaining sources proportionally so shares sum to 1 each year.
# Sensitivity: allow packaged growth to raise TOTAL sodium intake.
# Effect: packaged-targeting policies (FOPL, salt targets, fiscal) become
# progressively more consequential over time, without a 1:1 sales->sodium
# assumption.
```

# Fiscal-policy module (two methods)

Current code registers fiscal but sets the packaged effect to zero (comment says
10%).

**Primary — transparent fixed effect:**

```r
fiscal_effect_on_packaged_sodium <- 0.10   # provisional base case, RTSL to confirm
# Apply ONLY to packaged sodium in taxed nutrient-profile categories:
taxable_packaged_share <- <configurable>   # else the model implicitly taxes all packaged
```

**Structural sensitivity — elasticity model (Green et al. 2013):**

```r
# demand_ratio(c,k) = (1 + tax_rate(c) * pass_through(c)) ^ elasticity(c,k)
#
# sodium_reduction(c,t) = sum_over_k [
#   sodium(c,k,t) * tax_coverage(c,k) *
#   { 1 - (1 + tax_rate(c) * pass_through(c)) ^ elasticity(c,k) }
# ]
#
# Green income-stratified all-food elasticities ~ -0.74 (low), -0.68 (middle),
# -0.56 (high). Select by World Bank income tier.
```

Use the elasticity route as a **sensitivity**, not the whole fiscal effect: Green
does not supply the taxed sodium share, reformulation responses, cross-price
substitution, or category-specific sodium density.

# LSS redesign — replace, don't patch

Current LSS is a 15% discretionary reduction, zeroes normotensive BP bins, defines
eligibility by BP bin (not diagnosis/treatment), applies the restriction only when
LSS is the sole intervention (so it behaves **incorrectly inside a package**), and
ignores potassium.

## Scenarios and eligibility

```r
# lss_all           # scenario 2: whole-population discretionary (coverage toggle)
# lss_diagnosed_htn # scenario 4
# lss_treated_htn   # scenario 5
# Eligibility from HTN/HEARTS diagnosis & treatment coverage, NOT bp_cat >= 140.
```

## Eligibility x uptake x effectiveness (avoid >100% reach)

```r
# effective_reach =
#   eligible_population * availability * household_adoption * (1 - clinical_exclusion)
#
# Household spillover: use country-specific household size via a defined
# probability model. Do NOT multiply individual coverage by household size
# directly — that can exceed 100% and double-count households.
```

## SSaSS (Neal et al., NEJM 2021;385:1067-77) effect sizes

Trial context: cluster-RCT, 600 rural Chinese villages, 20,995 participants, mean
follow-up 4.74 y; prior stroke or ≥60 y with high BP; 75% NaCl / 25% KCl; supplied
for household use (so the effect reflects **household-level** exposure). SBP
−3.34 mmHg; urinary sodium −350 mg/day; urinary potassium **+803 mg/day**.

Clinical effects (RR, 95% CI):

```r
# Total stroke                 0.86 (0.77-0.96)
# MACE                         0.87 (0.80-0.94)
# All-cause death              0.88 (0.82-0.95)
# Vascular death               0.87 (0.79-0.96)
# Fatal stroke                 0.77 (0.65-0.91)
# Nonfatal stroke              0.90 (0.80-1.01)
# Ischemic stroke              0.93 (0.82-1.05)
# Hemorrhagic stroke           0.69 (0.56-0.85)
# Fatal/disabling stroke       0.84 (0.73-0.97)
# Nonfatal ACS                 0.70 (0.52-0.93)
# Serious hyperkalemia         1.04 (0.80-1.37)  # not statistically significant
```

Safety: the trial **excluded** known serious kidney disease, potassium-sparing
diuretics, potassium supplementation, and other household contraindications — so
apply a **configurable clinical-exclusion fraction** rather than the trial effect
to everyone.

## Mapping to the model — and the double-counting rule

`calculate_sodium_impact_etihad()` currently derives incidence effects via
Filippini SBP → ETIHAD RR (Steps 5–8) and holds case fatality neutral
(`CF_new := CF`, `eff_cf := 1`, Step 9). For the trial-based LSS path, bypass Steps
5–8 and apply SSaSS RRs directly to the reached, eligible population.

**Do NOT apply the total-stroke RR (0.86) to incidence AND the fatal-stroke RR
(0.77) to case fatality simultaneously** — the fatal-stroke RR already reflects the
combined effect on occurrence and fatality. Choose one coherent pathway:

```r
# A. Incidence pathway (PREFERRED base case — maps cleanly to IR/CF architecture):
#    stroke incidence multiplier = 0.86; leave case fatality unchanged unless a
#    conditional CF effect is formally derived.
#
# B. Outcome-specific pathway (sensitivity):
#    fatal stroke RR = 0.77; nonfatal stroke RR = 0.90; do NOT also apply 0.86 to incidence.
#
# C. Subtype pathway (sensitivity):
#    ischemic incidence RR = 0.93; hemorrhagic incidence RR = 0.69; do NOT also apply 0.86.
```

For total vascular mortality reporting, apply RR 0.87 to vascular mortality; use
all-cause RR 0.88 only in a separate validation/sensitivity run (the model focuses
on selected CVD causes).

## Primary vs sensitivity, and the second double-counting rule

```r
# PRIMARY   : trial-based RRs for the reached population (captures the combined
#             sodium-reduction + potassium-increase effect the team flagged as essential).
# SENSITIVITY: sodium->SBP method using the OBSERVED -3.34 mmHg (not reconstructed
#             from -350 mg/day alone; the +803 mg/day potassium drove much of the benefit).
# NEVER apply the direct trial RR AND the sodium-mediated SBP effect in the same
# scenario unless the trial effect has been decomposed — otherwise double-counted.
# Keep LSS scenarios OUT of full_package until the subgroup-specific implementation
# passes validation.
```

# Harmonising policy ramp-up

Effects in the evidence document were observed over very different periods; the
team asked for harmonisation. Store components separately:

```r
# policy_start_year
# full_implementation_year
# effect_reference_period
# curve_type
# full_effect
```

Base case: begin 2026, linear scale-up to full implementation in 2030, constant
after 2030. Treat each reported effect size as the **full-implementation effect**,
rather than mechanically converting every study result into an annual percentage.
Sensitivities: 3-year rapid, 5-year base, 7-year slow, and study-specific
realisation periods where justified. Apply the source trend and the intervention
ramp **separately** (see the engine equation above).

# Testing and validation

## Unit tests (`tests/testthat/`)

```r
# - source shares sum to 1 for every country-year
# - no source share or intervention effect is negative
# - inherent sodium is never targeted
# - parent and child Euromonitor categories are never both included
# - 2025 packaged index == 1
# - post-2030 trend behaviour matches the selected rule
# - overlapping effects use 1 - prod(1 - eff_i)
# - media absent from production scenarios
# - fiscal effect nonzero when enabled
# - LSS scenarios use diagnosed/treated eligibility correctly
# - household reach stays in [0, 1]
# - clinical exclusions applied BEFORE LSS effects
# - LSS stays subgroup-specific inside a combined scenario (the old bug)
# - direct LSS trial RRs and sodium/SBP effects never applied together
# - model results contain every configured year
```

## Regression tests

```r
# 1. Use the frozen MVP outputs for China (high discretionary) and Viet Nam
#    (high packaged) as the reference.
# 2. Refactor while preserving those outputs under a legacy_static config.
# 3. Only then activate new public-source, Euromonitor, fiscal, and LSS assumptions.
```

## External validation

```r
# - policy-specific sodium reductions vs the effect-size document
# - China LSS results vs SSaSS event rates and RRs
# - LSS country results vs selected TGI/SSaSS benchmarks
# - total deaths averted vs the earlier 100 Million Lives model
# - intervention rankings under static vs dynamic packaged-food shares
```

# Output audit trail

For every country × scenario × year, save:

```r
# baseline sodium intake; source-specific sodium amounts; source shares;
# Euromonitor trend index; eligible population; diagnosed/treated HTN coverage;
# household adoption; clinical-exclusion fraction; effective LSS reach; policy
# coverage; full intervention effect; implementation fraction; composed source
# effect; total sodium reduction; SBP reduction or direct RR; incidence multiplier;
# case-fatality multiplier; events and deaths averted.
```

Plus a machine-readable `assumptions_manifest.csv`:

```r
# config values; source files + versions; proxy-country decisions; trend method;
# fiscal method; LSS method; exact SSaSS RRs used; whether direct RRs or the SBP
# pathway were used; git commit id.
```

This prevents `salteff` from ever again becoming an opaque scalar and makes every
result explainable in the paper.

# Recommended implementation order

```r
# 1. Freeze and test current (MVP) outputs.
# 2. Centralise paths, years, countries, scenario controls in 00_run_model.R.
# 3. Move input construction into 02-03; make 07 a pure runner.
# 4. Remove media; disable LSS in full package; activate provisional fiscal.
# 5. Load revised adult public-procurement shares.
# 6. Add time-varying Euromonitor packaged-food shares.
# 7. Implement LSS 4 & 5 with household uptake, clinical exclusions, direct SSaSS RRs.
# 8. Add elasticity-based fiscal sensitivity.
# 9. Run regression, face-validity, and external benchmark checks.
```

# Main blocking inputs

Revised **adult public-procurement shares**; **Euromonitor aggregation weights**
(leaf categories + sodium density); **household-size / adoption** assumptions; and
the final decision on **which SSaSS outcome mapping** (A/B/C) is used in production.
Expose all of these as explicit inputs — never silently substitute ad hoc values.
